text:
alex: Heads-up — ran int8 bring-up for r3-rerank-v2 on the nightly bench. NDCG dropped ~3.6% on the longtail slice (queries > 90th pctile). MRR pretty flat. Anyone seen this pattern before?
mari: Ugh, that's sizable. Is the drop concentrated on any dataset or across anchors?
siva: Do you have the split by dataset? longtail could mean different doc lengths or candidate counts.
alex: Quick summary: offline eval vs goldset A. Split-by: core-sampled vs longtail-sampled. Longtail only shows the hit; core is +0.2%. I can paste the per-dataset table.
jordan: Could be formatting / priming differences. Int8 can slightly change score ordering for near-ties. Are we normalizing candidate text the same way as production?
alex: Table: 
- goldset-A-core: ndcg=0.823 -> 0.825 (int8)
- goldset-A-longtail: ndcg=0.731 -> 0.705 (int8)
- web-anchors: ndcg=0.788 -> 0.783
mari: Longtail drop looks real. How many queries in that slice? need to check significance.
siva: Sample sizes? bootstrap CI? If it's noisy maybe not worth blocking.
alex: Longtail slice n=4.2k queries. Bootstrap 95% CI on delta = [-0.048, -0.025] so looks significant.
jordan: Oof. Did you try disabling prefix KV caching or different batch sizes? Some quant kernels interact with kvpack and change order of scoring when candidates are very similar.
alex: Quick experiments: disabled kvpack and reran 500 queries — ndcg delta shrank to -0.6% but still negative. Batching smaller helped, but latency worsened.
siva: That suggests numerical perturbation from quant paths + prefix behavior. Two axes to investigate: (1) dataset preproc/format parity vs prod, (2) quantization config per-layer or hybrid FP16 for top layers.
mari: On (1) — I noticed we run `strip_html` and `normalize_unicode` in prod candidate pipeline. Are those applied in the eval harness? If not, ordering/score differences might be amplified for long documents.
jordan: Good call. Also check tokenization boundary differences — longtail queries often have punctuation/URLs. If tokenizer truncation differs between the harness and runtime kernels, embeddings/representations shift.
alex: I can re-run a small controlled test with exact prod preproc and tokenization. Command I used: 
```
./eval_harness --model r3-rerank-v2 --quant int8 --cohort longtail --num-queries 5000 --gold goldset-A
```
I'll add `--prod-preproc` flag and re-run.
ops-bot: Deploy note: r3-rerank-v2/int8 started on staging pool at 2024-10-12T09:12:00Z. No traffic routed.
mari: For (2), we should try hybrid-quant (int8 for most layers, fp16 for final 4). Historically that preserved top-of-rank ordering. Can we do a fast PTQ experiment?
siva: I'll spin a quick per-layer PTQ sweep this afternoon. If final layers keep higher precision, delta often disappears. I'll report back with ndcg by slice.
jordan: Also let's sanity-check candidate ordering: compute fraction of queries where top-1 changed between fp16 baseline and int8. If top-1 flips drive most of the ndcg loss then calibration/rescale fixes might help.
alex: Good idea. I'll produce a diff report with top-k flip counts and example failing queries (with original vs int8 ranking).
mari: If we find it's mostly ties, we can also try tiny score jitter tie-breaker that prefers higher-confidence candidates pre-quant. Not ideal but cheap.
siva: Action items: (a) alex: re-run harness with prod-preproc + tokenization parity (due today EOD) (b) siva: per-layer PTQ sweep (hybrid) (c) jordan: top-k flip report and candidate examples. We'll reconvene.
alex: Will post results in this thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:
